newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH SAILOR SET TO BREAK ROUND-THE-WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH SAILOR SET TO BREAK ROUND-THE-WORLD RECORD.

text.p: French sailor Olivier de Kersauzon raced for home on Sunday, heading to break New Zealander Sir Peter Blake's record for sailing round the world.
De Kersauzon radioed from his yacht Sport-Elec that he had sailed past Spain's Cape Finisterre overnight on the final stretch of his non-stop circumnavigation of the world.
De Kersauzon and his six French crew could cross the finishing line in the Channel on Monday to break by three days Blake's three-year-old record of 74 days 22 hours and 17 minutes.
Up to 100,000 fans were expected to welcome them in the French port of Brest which they left on March 4.
Blake, on his trimaran Enza-New Zealand, beat de Kersauzon in 1994 to take the Jules Verne trophy offered for sailing around the world in under 80 days.

Named after author Jules Verne's 1872 novel Around the World in 80 Days, the race ends at an imaginary line across the English Channel between the southernmost tip of Britain's Lizard Point and France's Ouessant Island.
Blake had broken a record of 79 days six hours and 15 minutes set a year earlier by France's Bruno Peyron on his trimaran Commodore explorer.
